title: Requirements Analysis and Specification — Question Bank

MCQ.description: Multiple Choice Questions — choose the single best answer

questions.question: What does Requirements Engineering (RE) primarily produce?

options.B: A large natural-language document describing what the system will do
options.C: A database schema for the system
options.D: A test suite for the final software

questions.explanation: RE produces one large document written in natural language containing a description of what the system will do.

questions.question: Which of the following best describes a User Requirement?

options.A: A detailed specification of system functions written in technical language
options.B: A high-level abstract statement written in natural language with diagrams
options.C: A structured document listing function signatures and API contracts
options.D: A performance metric measured in milliseconds

questions.explanation: User requirements are high-level abstract requirements written in natural language plus diagrams describing services and operational constraints.

questions.question: Which of the following is a functional requirement for the MHC-PMS?

options.A: The system shall be available Mon–Fri from 0830 to 17:30
options.B: Each staff member shall be identified by an 8-digit employee number
options.C: Downtime shall not exceed five seconds in any one day
options.D: Users shall authenticate using a health authority identity card

questions.explanation: Staff identification by employee number describes what the system does — a functional requirement. The rest are non-functional (availability, downtime, authentication policy).

questions.question: Non-functional requirements typically apply to:

options.B: The system as a whole rather than individual features or services
options.C: Only the user interface layer
options.D: Only the database layer

questions.explanation: Non-functional requirements often apply to the system as a whole rather than individual features — e.g., reliability, performance.

questions.question: A requirement that can be verified using an objective measure is called:

options.B: A domain requirement
options.C: A verifiable non-functional requirement
options.D: A user story

questions.explanation: A verifiable non-functional requirement uses some measure that can be objectively tested, unlike a goal which is a general intention like ease of use.

questions.question: System requirements are primarily intended for which audience?

options.B: Developers, testers, and system architects
options.C: Government regulatory bodies
options.D: Marketing and sales teams

questions.explanation: System requirements target developers, testers, client engineers, and system architects — they are detailed and technical.

questions.question: Domain requirements are derived from:

options.B: The application domain of the system rather than specific user needs
options.C: The programming language chosen for development
options.D: The end-user interface wireframes

questions.explanation: Domain requirements come from the application domain itself — e.g., braking characteristics for a train control system — not from specific user requests.

questions.question: Which is an example of an Organisational non-functional requirement?

options.A: The system shall process 500 transactions per second
options.B: The system shall comply with GDPR regulations
options.C: The system shall be developed using the Python programming language
options.D: The system shall have a mean time to failure of 1000 hours

questions.explanation: Specifying a programming language is an organisational requirement derived from development process policies.

questions.question: The MHC-PMS is designed to also run locally on a PC so that:

options.A: It can be sold as standalone commercial software
options.B: It can be accessed from sites without secure network connectivity
options.C: It avoids cloud computing costs
options.D: Patients can access it directly at home

questions.explanation: MHC-PMS was designed to run on a PC so it can be used from sites that do not have secure network connectivity.

questions.question: Why is it practically impossible to produce a complete and consistent requirements document?

options.B: Stakeholder conflicts, changing needs, and system complexity make gaps and contradictions unavoidable
options.C: Natural language is too expressive
options.D: Requirements tools are not sophisticated enough

questions.explanation: In practice, stakeholder conflicts and the complexity of capturing all system interactions make truly complete and consistent requirements impossible.

questions.question: In MHC-PMS, the requirement 'A user shall be able to search the appointments list for all clinics' caused ambiguity because:

options.B: The word 'search' was interpreted differently by users and developers
options.C: The word 'appointments' was too technical
options.D: The requirement was written in a programming language

questions.explanation: The user intended cross-clinic search simultaneously; the developer interpreted it as selecting a clinic first then searching — both interpretations of 'search'.

questions.question: For the Reliability property, which is a valid metric for specifying a non-functional requirement?

options.B: Percentage of target-dependent statements
options.C: Mean time to failure
options.D: Number of help frames

questions.explanation: Mean time to failure, probability of unavailability, and rate of failure occurrence are all metrics for the Reliability property as listed in the document.

questions.question: A single security non-functional requirement can generate which of the following?

options.B: Related functional requirements defining required services and constraints on existing requirements
options.C: Only user interface mockups
options.D: Only test plans

questions.explanation: A single NFR like security may spawn multiple related functional requirements and may also restrict or constrain existing functional requirements.

questions.question: According to Davis's principle, why must requirements be written abstractly before a contract is awarded?

options.B: So that several contractors can bid, each offering potentially different approaches
options.C: To avoid legal liability for the client
options.D: Because natural language is always vague

questions.explanation: Requirements must be abstract enough to allow multiple contractors to bid with different approaches without pre-defining a single solution.

questions.question: Why can non-functional requirements be more critical than functional requirements?

options.B: If unmet, the entire system may become useless even if all functional requirements are met
options.C: They are always cheaper to implement
options.D: They are mandated by government regulations

questions.explanation: A system can satisfy all functional requirements but still be useless if it is too slow, unreliable, or insecure — making NFRs potentially more critical.

questions.question: Which of the following is a testable usability non-functional requirement for MHC-PMS?

options.A: The system should be easy to use by medical staff
options.B: User errors should be minimized
options.C: Medical staff shall use all system functions after four hours of training, with no more than two errors per hour thereafter
options.D: The interface should be friendly

questions.explanation: Four-hours training and a maximum of two errors per hour are measurable and objectively testable — a verifiable NFR. The others are vague goals.

questions.question: Which characteristic ensures requirements do not contradict one another?

options.B: Feasibility
options.C: Consistency
options.D: Modifiability

questions.explanation: Consistent requirements prevent conflicts and confusion — there should be no contradictions in descriptions of system facilities.

questions.question: According to MHC-PMS system requirement 1.2, when is the monthly management report automatically generated?

options.A: On the first working day of each month at 09:00
options.B: After 17:30 on the last working day of each month
options.C: Every Friday at midnight
options.D: Whenever the clinic manager requests it

questions.explanation: System requirement 1.2 states the report shall be automatically generated for printing after 17:30 on the last working day of the month.

questions.question: A performance NFR requiring minimal response time is most likely to impact the system architecture in which way?

options.A: It will only affect the user interface layer
options.B: It may require reorganizing the entire system to minimize inter-component communication
options.C: It will only affect the database schema
options.D: NFRs have no architectural implications

questions.explanation: NFRs can affect the overall architecture. To meet performance requirements, the whole system may need to be reorganized to minimize communications between components.

questions.question: A domain requirement for a financial system specifies a margin-call formula in domain-specific financial notation. A software engineer misinterprets it. This is an example of which domain requirement problem?

options.A: Implicitness — the domain expert assumed the engineer knew the formula
options.B: Understandability — the requirement is expressed in domain language not understood by the engineer
options.C: Completeness — the formula was not fully specified
options.D: Consistency — the formula contradicts another requirement

questions.explanation: This is an understandability problem — domain requirements in specialised application-domain language are often not understood by software engineers developing the system.

questions.question: A hospital issues a 2-page abstract requirements document for tendering, then after awarding the contract the contractor writes a 200-page detailed specification. Which statement best describes this?

options.A: The 2-page document is invalid since requirements must be detailed
options.B: Both documents can legitimately be called the requirements document, serving different purposes at different contract stages
options.C: The 200-page document replaces the 2-page document entirely
options.D: Only the 200-page document satisfies the Davis definition of requirements

questions.explanation: Davis states both forms are valid requirements documents. The abstract version enables open bidding; the detailed version defines exactly what will be built.

questions.question: A stakeholder demands that a web application respond to every user click within 10 milliseconds globally, regardless of geography. Which requirement characteristic is most critically violated?

options.B: Unambiguity
options.C: Feasibility
options.D: Modifiability

questions.explanation: Feasibility requires requirements to align with project constraints and avoid unrealistic expectations. A 10ms global response time violates physical network latency limits, making it infeasible.

questions.question: The requirement 'The MHC-PMS shall implement patient privacy provisions as set out in HStan-03-2006-priv' is classified as which type of non-functional requirement?

options.B: Organisational requirement
options.C: External requirement
options.D: Efficiency requirement

questions.explanation: This is an External requirement — it derives from factors external to the system and its development process, specifically a legislative/regulatory privacy standard.

questions.question: According to the metrics table, which measures are used to specify Portability as a non-functional property?

options.A: Mean time to failure and probability of unavailability
options.B: Training time and number of help frames
options.C: Percentage of target-dependent statements and number of target systems
options.D: Processed transactions per second and screen refresh time

questions.explanation: The portability metrics listed are: percentage of target-dependent statements and number of target systems the software can run on.

questions.question: Requirements Engineering is best described as a sub-discipline of software engineering concerned with:

options.A: Writing code that matches a given architecture
options.B: Determining the goals, functions, and constraints of software systems
options.C: Testing software against user acceptance criteria
options.D: Deploying software to production environments

questions.explanation: RE is the sub-discipline of software engineering concerned with determining the goals, functions, and constraints of software systems.

TrueFalse.description: True or False — state whether the given statement is correct

questions.question: Requirements Engineering means that requirements for a product are defined, managed, and tested/validated systematically.
questions.explanation: This is the exact definition of Requirements Engineering as given in the slides.

questions.question: Functional requirements describe HOW the system should perform, while non-functional requirements describe WHAT the system should do.
questions.explanation: It is the opposite. Functional requirements describe WHAT the system should do; non-functional requirements describe HOW the system should perform.

questions.question: User requirements are always written in formal mathematical notation to avoid ambiguity.
questions.explanation: User requirements are written in natural language plus diagrams — not formal notation. They are high-level and abstract.

questions.question: When MHC-PMS local systems are disconnected from the network, they can download and use local copies of patient records.
questions.explanation: The slides explicitly state that local systems can download and use local copies of patient records when disconnected.

questions.question: System requirements are primarily written for end-users and client managers to read.
questions.explanation: System requirements target developers, testers, client engineers, and system architects — not primarily end-users and managers, who read user requirements.

questions.question: Domain requirements are derived from the specific personal needs of system end-users.
questions.explanation: Domain requirements come from the application domain itself, not from the specific needs of system users.

questions.question: Testable requirements ensure the system can be validated, reducing the risk of implementation errors.
questions.explanation: Testable requirements allow objective validation that the system meets specified criteria, reducing implementation risk.

questions.question: Non-functional requirements can never be more critical than functional requirements.
questions.explanation: The slides explicitly state that non-functional requirements may be MORE critical than functional requirements — if unmet, the system may be useless.

questions.question: One of the MHC-PMS goals is to provide medical staff with timely information to support patient treatment.
questions.explanation: This is explicitly stated as one of the two MHC-PMS goals in the slides.

questions.question: In principle, requirements should be both complete and consistent, but in practice it is impossible to achieve both simultaneously.
questions.explanation: The slides state that while requirements should ideally be complete and consistent, in practice it is impossible to produce a document that is fully both.

questions.question: A goal and a verifiable non-functional requirement are essentially the same thing.
questions.explanation: A goal is a general intention (e.g., ease of use) while a verifiable NFR uses a measurable metric that can be objectively tested. They are distinctly different.

questions.question: Organisational non-functional requirements are a consequence of organisational policies and procedures, such as specifying the development programming language.
questions.explanation: Organisational requirements derive from organisational policies — they can include how the system will be used or what language to use.

questions.question: A non-functional requirement like performance only affects individual components, never the overall system architecture.
questions.explanation: NFRs may affect the overall architecture of a system rather than individual components — performance may require restructuring the whole system.

questions.question: According to MHC-PMS system requirement 1.5, access to all cost reports is open to any authenticated staff member.
questions.explanation: Requirement 1.5 states access to cost reports is restricted to authorized users listed on a management access control list — not all authenticated staff.

questions.question: Ambiguous requirements are always interpreted the same way by both developers and users.
questions.explanation: Ambiguous requirements may be interpreted in different ways by developers and users — this is precisely the problem of requirements imprecision.

questions.question: After a contract is awarded, the contractor must write a more detailed system definition so the client can understand and validate what the software will do.
questions.explanation: Per Davis's principle, once a contract is awarded the contractor writes a detailed system definition for client validation.

questions.question: If domain requirements are not satisfied, the system may be unworkable.
questions.explanation: The slides explicitly state that if domain requirements are not satisfied, the system may be unworkable.

questions.question: Screen refresh time is a valid metric for specifying the Speed property of a non-functional requirement.
questions.explanation: The metrics table lists processed transactions/second, user/event response time, and screen refresh time as metrics for Speed.

questions.question: A single non-functional security requirement can generate multiple functional requirements that define the system services needed to enforce that security.
questions.explanation: The slides state a single NFR like security may generate related functional requirements defining required services and may also restrict existing requirements.

questions.question: Modifiable requirements mean the system itself is easy to modify at runtime — not the requirements document.
questions.explanation: Modifiable requirements refer to the requirements document being structured so requirements can be changed over time — it is a property of the requirements specification, not the running system.

questions.question: Domain experts sometimes fail to make domain requirements explicit because they assume the knowledge is obvious to everyone involved.
questions.explanation: This is the implicitness problem — domain specialists understand the area so well they do not think of making domain requirements explicit.

questions.question: The train deceleration formula Dtrain = Dcontrol + Dgradient is easy for a non-specialist software engineer to understand and implement without domain guidance.
questions.explanation: The slides explicitly state it is difficult for a non-specialist to understand the implications of this formula and how it interacts with other requirements.

questions.question: Probability of data corruption on failure is listed as a valid metric for measuring the Robustness property in non-functional requirements.
questions.explanation: The three Robustness metrics are: time to restart after failure, percentage of events causing failure, and probability of data corruption on failure.

questions.question: The MHC-PMS product requirement stating the system shall be available Mon–Fri 0830–17:30 with downtime not exceeding five seconds per day is a verifiable non-functional requirement.
questions.explanation: It is verifiable because availability hours and the five-second downtime cap are measurable metrics — it qualifies as both a product requirement and a verifiable NFR.

questions.question: Functional system requirements should provide high-level abstract descriptions, leaving detailed implementation decisions to the developer's discretion.
questions.explanation: Functional system requirements should describe system services IN DETAIL. It is user requirements that are high-level and abstract.

FillInTheBlanks.description: Fill in the blank with the most appropriate word or phrase from the course content

questions.question: Requirements Engineering is a sub-discipline of software engineering concerned with determining the goals, __________, and constraints of software systems.
questions.explanation: RE determines the goals, functions, and constraints of software systems.

questions.question: Software system requirements are often classified as either __________ requirements or non-functional requirements.
questions.explanation: The two primary classifications are functional and non-functional requirements.

questions.question: User requirements are statements written in __________ language plus diagrams of the services the system provides.
questions.explanation: User requirements use natural language, making them accessible to non-technical stakeholders.

questions.question: The MHC-PMS makes use of a __________ database of patient information.
questions.explanation: The MHC-PMS uses a centralized database while also supporting local PC operation.

questions.question: Software Requirements are the wants and needs of the __________.
questions.explanation: Requirements directly reflect what stakeholders want and need from the system.

questions.question: Requirements Engineering produces a large document written in natural language that contains a description of __________ the system will do.
questions.explanation: The RE document describes what the system will do — not how it will be built.

questions.question: Functional requirements describe the __________ or system services the software must provide.
questions.explanation: Functional requirements describe functionality or system services.

questions.question: __________ requirements prevent conflicts and confusion between different parts of the specification.
questions.explanation: Consistency ensures there are no contradictions in the descriptions of system facilities.

questions.question: According to MHC-PMS system requirement 1.2, the monthly management report shall be automatically generated for printing after __________ on the last working day of the month.
questions.explanation: Requirement 1.2 specifies 17:30 as the trigger time for automatic report generation.

questions.question: Non-functional requirements are classified into three categories: Product requirements, __________ requirements, and External requirements.
questions.explanation: The three NFR classifications are Product, Organisational, and External requirements.

questions.question: If domain requirements are not satisfied, the system may be __________.
questions.explanation: The slides state unsatisfied domain requirements can render the system unworkable.

questions.question: Ambiguous requirements may be interpreted in different ways by __________ and users, leading to implementation mismatches.
questions.explanation: The slides warn that ambiguous requirements are interpreted differently by developers versus users.

questions.question: A __________ is a general intention of the user, such as ease of use, which is helpful to developers as it conveys user intent.
questions.explanation: Goals convey the intentions of system users to developers, even if they are not precisely testable.

questions.question: For the Ease of Use property, the two metrics listed are training time and number of __________ frames.
questions.explanation: The metrics table lists training time and number of help frames as measures for ease of use.

questions.question: In MHC-PMS, each staff member using the system shall be uniquely identified by his or her __________ employee number.
questions.explanation: The functional requirement specifies an 8-digit employee number for unique staff identification.

questions.question: The two key problems with domain requirements are __________ and implicitness.
questions.explanation: Understandability (domain language unfamiliar to engineers) and implicitness (experts assume knowledge is obvious) are the two domain requirement problems.

questions.question: __________ requirements ensure no functionality or system attribute is overlooked in the specification.
questions.explanation: Completeness ensures all required functionality and system attributes are captured.

questions.question: The MHC-PMS external non-functional requirement states the system shall implement patient privacy provisions as set out in __________.
questions.explanation: This is the specific privacy standard cited in the MHC-PMS non-functional requirements example.

questions.question: System requirements define what should be implemented and may be part of a __________ between client and contractor.
questions.explanation: System requirements can form part of the formal contract between client and contractor.

questions.question: Non-functional requirements may affect the overall __________ of a system rather than its individual components.
questions.explanation: NFRs like performance can require whole-system architectural changes, not just component-level modifications.

questions.question: In the train protection system domain requirement, the deceleration formula is: Dtrain = Dcontrol + __________.
questions.explanation: The formula from the slides is Dtrain = Dcontrol + Dgradient, where Dgradient accounts for gradient-based deceleration.

questions.question: A verifiable non-functional requirement is a statement using some __________ that can be objectively tested.
questions.explanation: Verifiable NFRs rely on a concrete measure — unlike goals which are subjective intentions.

questions.question: One of the three metrics for specifying Robustness as a non-functional property is the probability of __________ on failure.
questions.explanation: The three Robustness metrics are: time to restart after failure, percentage of events causing failure, and probability of data corruption on failure.

questions.question: According to MHC-PMS system requirement 1.4, if drugs are available in different __________ units, separate reports shall be created for each.
questions.explanation: Requirement 1.4 specifies that drugs available in different dose units (e.g., 10 mg, 20 mg) each require a separate report.

questions.question: __________ requirements align with project constraints, avoiding unrealistic expectations from stakeholders.
questions.explanation: Feasibility ensures requirements can realistically be implemented within the project's technical and budget constraints.
